meta.name: Hyperproof
meta.title: Hyperproof ad teardown: two hooks in one ad, and the page picks the right one
meta.meta_desc: A teardown of Hyperproof’s LinkedIn ad: “CISO for a Day” is a strong offer, the creative leads with a different line, and the page delivers the game with one proof point near the bottom.
meta.og_desc: Two hooks in one ad. The page picks the right one.

hook: The page picks the right one.
voice.lede: Hyperproof turned a 15-question maturity quiz into a game, and that is a real offer. “CISO for a Day” is a stronger idea than almost anything else in GRC advertising. The ad just does not commit to it: the creative shouts “The Proof Is In the Platform,” the headline says something else, and the button under both says “Learn more.” The page knows what it is, and it is the best part of this funnel.

findings.title: Two hooks compete for one glance
findings.what: The creative says “The Proof Is In the Platform.” The headline says “CISO for a Day: Play the Scenarios, Get Your Score.” The reader has to decide which one the ad is about.
findings.fix: Lead the creative with “CISO for a Day.” It is the offer, and the slogan is not.

findings.title: A specific promise
findings.what: “9 real scenarios, one GRC maturity score” tells the reader the size of the commitment and exactly what they get at the end. Most compliance ads never get this concrete.

findings.title: “Learn more” undersells a game
findings.what: The creative’s own button says “Play CISO for a Day.” LinkedIn’s button says “Learn more.” Nobody learns more from a game, they play it.
findings.fix: Match the written call to action to the creative’s button.

findings.title: No proof in the ad
findings.what: There is no customer name, logo or number on the creative. The page has an Acuity International story, and the ad doesn’t use it.
findings.fix: Add the Acuity result as one line on the creative.

findings.title: The buyer’s day, in two sentences
findings.what: “Your board wants answers, your auditor wants evidence, and your third-party vendor list just doubled” is the ICP’s week, written in the game’s own voice.

findings.title: “Start my shift” keeps the game going
findings.what: The button stays inside the role-play, where a generic “Start now” would break it. It is a small choice that makes the whole page feel designed.

findings.title: One proof point, far from the button
findings.what: Acuity International and its “1/3 of the time” result sit far below the first call to action. It is the only proof on the page.
findings.fix: Move the Acuity number up beside “Start my shift” and add two or three logos.

faq.q: What is wrong with Hyperproof’s LinkedIn ad?
faq.a: It has a great offer and does not lead with it. The creative’s slogan and the “CISO for a Day” headline compete, and “Learn more” undersells an interactive game.

faq.q: What does the landing page do well?
faq.a: It stays in character. The copy speaks to the buyer’s real week, “Start my shift” keeps the role-play going, and the “What you get” list says exactly what comes out of the game.

faq.q: Why does an interactive assessment beat a static quiz here?
faq.a: It answers from decisions rather than self-reported ratings, and that makes the score more believable. The ad should say so, because “no 15-question quiz required” is a real difference.

issues.title: Headline Clarity
issues.explanation: Creative says 'The Proof Is In the Platform' but ad copy headline is 'CISO for a Day: Play the Scenarios, Get Your Score.' Two different hooks competing for attention.

issues.title: CTA Friction
issues.explanation: 'Learn more' is soft for an interactive game offer. Creative's own button says 'Play CISO for a Day,' which is punchier and matches intent better.

issues.title: Visual-Copy Match
issues.explanation: Creative headline 'The Proof Is In the Platform' never appears in ad copy text, and copy's 'no 15-question quiz required' isn't echoed on the creative at all.

issues.title: Benefit Specificity
issues.explanation: '9 real scenarios, one GRC maturity score' is concrete and specific, a real step up from vague 'improve your compliance posture' filler.

issues.title: Trust Signals
issues.explanation: No customer name, logo, or proof point in the ad itself, LinkedIn supports it but this creative skips it entirely.
